summary: Marie-Thérèse de Mallmann worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned diplomas from the École du Louvre and École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under Foucher, Przyluski, Mus, Hackin, Grousset, and Stern. She held posts at the CNRS (1942–1974) and Guimet Museum (1948–1975).

Marielle Harrison specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Washington and the University of Chicago (MA). She served as a Teaching Fellow at Chicago (2025–2026) and became an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University in 2026.

Mariia Lepneva works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations and Buryat State University. Lepneva held positions as a Chinese teacher, translator, senior specialist at Vi Holding, and postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2023–2026).

Marijan Molé specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at Ljubljana, the Jagiellonian University (PhD), and EPHE, he studied under Oštir, Safarewicz, Willman-Grabowska, Benveniste, and de Menasce. He held posts at Jagiellonian, CNRS (1950–1955), and IFRI (1955–1959).

Marilyn Hirsh worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She studied at Carnegie Mellon University (~1961–1965) and taught Indian and Buddhist art at the Cooper Union and the Institute of Fine Arts, New York University.

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University by 2006, where she studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Marina Rimscha works in Indology and linguistics. She completed an MA and Dr. Phil. at the University of Bonn. Her posts include teaching and research roles at Bonn, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, University of Haifa, and Technion – Israel Institute of Technology.

Mario Bonardi worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Carlo Formichi and Giuseppe Tucci (~1933–1938) and held posts at the Sapienza University of Rome and the Italian Institute for Africa and the East.

Mario Bussagli was an Italian scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci at Sapienza University of Rome (~1936–1940), where he later served as a Docent from 1957 to 1987.

Mario Cappieri was a scholar in Indology and archaeology. He served as a Lecturer in Demography at Sapienza University of Rome and became Professor of Anthropology at the University of Naples Federico II in 1955.

Mario D'Amato specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1994–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths. He held positions at Hampshire College (~2000–2005) and Rollins College (~2005).
Mario Daza de Campos was an Indology scholar who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. Beginning in 1897, he served as Ordinary Professor of Sanskrit at the Complutense University of Madrid.

Mario Poceski is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He taught at the University of Iowa (2001) before joining the University of Florida faculty in 2001.

Mario Praz studied at the University of Bologna (~1915–1918) and the University of Florence (~1918–1920). He later held posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).

Mario Vallauri was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michele Kerbaker at Naples, Paolo Emilio Pavolini at Florence, and Julius Jolly at Würzburg. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Turin as a libero docente (1922) and lecturer (1924–1931).

Marion L. Matics worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Matics completed a PhD at Columbia University in 1960 under Horace L. Friess and Robert A. Fowkes, and later taught Oriental philosophy at Columbia University and Brooklyn College.

Marion Meyer is an archaeologist who earned her PhD at the University of Bonn (1975–1984). She held academic posts at the University of Hamburg, University of Bonn (1997–2003), and University of Vienna, where she was Full Professor from 2003 to 2020.

Marion Rastelli is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer. She has held affiliations with the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and the University of Vienna as a lecturer (attested 2020–2026).
Marius Zemp specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He completed a Lizentiat at the University of Bern (1999–2014) and served as a lecturer there from 2020 to 2025.

Mark A. Nathan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and has held positions at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).
